title: Frazier v. Nashville Presbytery
disposition_detail: Single issue—whether Nashville Presbytery erred at its 87th Stated Meeting by finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt under BCO 31-2 and declining process against TE Scott Sauls—answered No; the Complaint was denied. The SJC adopted reasoning that the 147-page Record showed Presbytery fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duties and did not show error in judgment declining to proceed to charges. Concurring opinions raised recusal, record-clarity, and exegetical concerns, but no separate dissent affected the denial.
first_summary: The SJC denied a complaint against Nashville Presbytery's refusal to indict a minister for teaching on same-sex attraction. The Commission found the record supported Presbytery's BCO 31-2 investigation and judgment. The complaint was denied.
summary: The SJC denied a complaint challenging Nashville Presbytery's decision not to indict a teaching elder for allegedly sinful teaching on homosexuality and same-sex attraction. The adopted judgment held that the 147-page record showed Presbytery fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duty and did not show it erred in judgment when it declined process; the complaint was denied 20-0-1. Concurring opinions raised concerns about committee recusal, record clarity, and exegetical uses of Scripture, but they were separate and did not alter the denial.
